issue.title: Probes parse localized output: non-English hosts get a false `failed_logins`, and certificate dates go unparsed

labels.name: reliability
labels.description: Correctness under concurrency, retries, and timing

issue.body:
## Problem

Only the two journal probes pin the locale, with `environment: LC_ALL: C` (`roles/vitals_scan/tasks/log_errors.yml:24-25` and `kernel_install_failures.yml:31-32`). Every other probe runs in whatever locale the SSH session has, and Ansible doesn't reset it. At start-up `AnsibleModule` calls `locale.setlocale(locale.LC_ALL, '')`, which adopts the session's `LANG`/`LC_*`. Managed hosts routinely run in a non-English locale. Debian and Ubuntu apply `/etc/default/locale` to SSH sessions through `pam_env`, and common `ssh_config`/`sshd_config` defaults forward `LANG` and `LC_*` from the operator's machine.

Three parsers assume English output:

1. **`failed_logins` fires on hosts with no failed logins.** `lastb` ends its output with `btmp begins <date>`, and `extended_facts.yml:143` and `:152` drop that line with `reject('match', '^btmp begins ')`. The trailer is translated: util-linux `login-utils/last.c`, msgid `"\n%s begins %s\n"`, is `beginnt` in de, `commence` in fr and `empieza` in es. On a host with an empty `btmp` running under `de_DE.UTF-8`, the probe prints `btmp beginnt …`, which gets past the filter. The result:
   - `failed_login_count` is 1, and `last_failed_login` is the trailer;
   - `result.yml:53` raises `failed_logins`, which fails the host under the default `linux_vitals_fail_on_severity: info`;
   - on a host with real entries, the count is one too high.
2. **Certificate dates are not parsed, and an expired certificate is reported clean.** `plugins/modules/linux_vitals_cert_facts.py:149` parses openssl's `notAfter` with `strptime("%b %d %H:%M:%S %Y")`. openssl always prints English month abbreviations, but `%b` matches the module process's `LC_TIME`.
   - Under glibc's `de_DE` the abbreviations include `Mär`, `Mai`, `Okt` and `Dez`, so a certificate dated in March, May, October or December doesn't parse. Under `fr_FR` and `es_ES` most months fail.
   - `_parse_openssl_time` then returns `None`, and the module sets `not_after`, `days_remaining` and `expired` to `None` (`:241-243`).
   - `roles/vitals_certs/tasks/main.yml:88-110` raises nothing for such a certificate: no `cert_expired`, no `cert_expiring`, and it isn't counted in the summary's `expired`.

   Reproduced by calling `_parse_openssl_time` after `locale.setlocale(locale.LC_ALL, 'de_DE.UTF-8')`, which returns `None` for `Dec 31 23:59:59 2024 GMT`. Rendering the findings template for the resulting certificate on ansible-core 2.20.4 gives `[]`. The default scan paths include the CA bundle (`/etc/ssl/certs`), so every such host has affected certificates.
3. **`last_reboot` keeps the localized label.** coreutils translates `who -b`'s `system boot`, and `extended_facts.yml:160` strips only the English one. This one is display-only.

## Proposed fix

- Add `environment: {LC_ALL: C}` to every `ansible.builtin.command` probe in `roles/vitals_scan/tasks/`, and to the `systemctl` calls in `vitals_heal` for consistency. Add a test that fails when a probe task has no `LC_ALL`, in the same ratchet style as `REVIEWED_PROBES_THAT_IGNORE_FAILURE`.
- In the cert module, parse dates without depending on the locale. Either use a fixed English month table instead of `%b`, or force a C `LC_TIME` around the parse. Add a unit test that parses all twelve months under a non-C locale.
- A certificate whose dates can't be parsed must not read as clean. Raise an `unknown` finding with the raw date in its `reason` (#62; pairs with #119).
- `who -b` under `LC_ALL=C` prints `Mon DD HH:MM` with no year. Consider deriving `last_reboot` from `ansible_facts.uptime_seconds` instead.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every scan probe runs with `LC_ALL=C`, and a test enforces it
- [ ] An empty `btmp` under a non-English locale raises no `failed_logins` (golden fixture with a localized trailer)
- [ ] `_parse_openssl_time` parses all twelve months under `de_DE.UTF-8` and `fr_FR.UTF-8`
- [ ] A certificate with unparseable dates produces an `unknown` finding, not silence
- [ ] `last_reboot` isn't localized

Related: #39 rewrites the same `lastb` probe for its unknown paths, and #119 covers unknowns in `vitals_certs`.
